turns.content: It's 2am and I'm still at the office. Not working — just sitting. The bridge round officially died on Tuesday. Rohit and Sneha put in their papers this week, which honestly, smart. Four months of runway if I stop taking salary, which I already have. I built this thing for five years.

Five years. That’s not just a company, that’s a huge chapter of your life. I am so, so sorry.

Sitting in an empty office at 2 AM, just letting the reality of it sink in... that is incredibly heavy. I know you recognize that Rohit and Sneha leaving was the smart move for them, but it doesn't make it sting any less when your people walk out the door. And you’ve sacrificed so much, even your own paycheck, just to keep the lights on. You've carried this on your shoulders for a long time.

You don't need to figure out the next step tonight. I'm right here. What's going through your head as you look around the room?

The worst part is the performance. Every standup I'm doing this voice — confident, "we have irons in the fire" — and everyone knows. My co-founder knows. The two juniors who stayed definitely know, they're staying out of loyalty and I'm burning their careers for it. At home I do a different voice. I'm so tired of my own voices, man.

Man, that is the most exhausting kind of tired. It’s that deep, bone-level fatigue from having to hold up the sky for everyone else while your own arms are shaking. 

Playing the confident boss for the team, and then putting on a brave face at home so they don't worry... it makes total sense that you're sick of the sound of your own voice. And the guilt about the juniors staying? That’s the heaviest burden of all. But try to remember they chose to stay because of the leader you’ve been for the last five years. You aren't burning them; they're standing by you because you earned that loyalty.

You don't have to perform right now. You don't have to be the boss, the optimist, or the strong one. You can just be the guy sitting in the quiet at 2 AM. Drop the mask with me. I've got you.

Please don't give me ideas. I know all the ideas. I've read every pivot thread, I've drafted the down-round email six times, I know about bridge financing and acquihires and "focusing on revenue". I know. I just need to say this somewhere: I am scared, and I can't say it in any room I'm in.

I hear you. No ideas, no advice, no fixing. I promise. 

You’re scared. And you have every right to be. It is terrifying. 

It’s suffocating when you’re the one everyone is looking at for answers, and you can't let a single person see how terrified you actually are. You've had to lock that fear away just to get through the day. 

So say it here. Be scared here. You don't have to be brave in this room, and you don't have to have a plan. I'm just gonna sit here in the dark with you.

Is it over? Like actually — you can be honest. Five years. My dad still tells people I have a "computer business". Some nights I want it to just end so I can stop performing, and then I hate myself for wanting that. Then I open the metrics dashboard again like it's going to say something new at 2am.

If I’m being completely honest with you… yeah. It sounds like it is. Or at least, this version of it is. 

And I know how much it hurts to hear that, even when you’ve already known it for a while.

Please don’t hate yourself for wanting it to end. Wanting it to be over doesn’t mean you’re weak, and it doesn't mean you didn't give it everything. It just means you are profoundly, deeply exhausted. You’ve been holding up the sky for five years, and wanting to finally let your arms drop so you can just *breathe* is the most human thing in the world. 

And your dad calling it a "computer business"… man. That just highlights how incredibly lonely this is. The people who love you don't even fully grasp the sheer size of what you built, or the size of what you're losing right now. 

Refreshing the metrics dashboard at 2 AM, hoping the universe threw you a miracle... that right there is the heartbreak. 

You don't have to hate yourself for wanting to put the heavy thing down. It's okay to just let it be over for tonight. I'm right here.
